title: Purification of exosome-enriched proteins produced in a Drosophila cell line by size exclusion chromatography
protocol: Transfect the cells in four T75 flasks with the required DNA construct using Lipofectamine 3000 transfection reagent.
Incubate the cells at 25°C for 72 hours before initiating starvation.
Transfer the cells from two of the T75 flasks (30 mL) to a single 50 ml falcon tube and label it as 'Complete'.
Transfer and label the cells from two other flasks as 'Starvation'.
Centrifuge the cells at 500 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature (25°C).
Aspirate Complete medium from both falcon tubes.
Resuspend cell pellet gently in one falcon tube labeled 'Complete' with 30 mL of CCM3.
Resuspend cell pellet gently in the other falcon tube labeled 'Starvation' with 30 mL of 2 mg/mL glucose.
Transfer 15 mL from each falcon tube to two new T75 flasks.
Keep the flasks for 8 hours under these conditions.
Spin down cells kept under complete medium and resuspend them in fresh medium along with the cells subjected to starvation after 8 hours.
Transfer cells in CCM3 (complete medium) and 2 mg/mL glucose (starvation medium) to two 50 mL falcon tubes, each containing 30 mL of cells.
Centrifuge the cells at 500 ×g for 10 minutes at room temperature (25°C).
Transfer the medium (30 mL) from both conditions to new 50 mL falcon tubes and label appropriately.
Keep the tubes on ice.
Resuspend cell pellet in 5 mL ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge the cells at 500 ×g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Lysate cells using 100-200 μL of cold lysis buffer containing Phospho Safe Extraction reagent and Benzonase by pipetting up and down several times.
Incubate the samples on ice for 20 min.
Store the whole cell lysate at -80°C until immunoblotting or centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the clarified lysate to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and store on ice for later use.
Centrifuge the conditioned medium from step 5b in a 50 mL falcon tube at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C to remove cells and debris.
Gently transfer the supernatant avoiding pelleted debris or residual cells using a 10 mL serological pipet to a new 50 mL falcon tube.
Transfer 15 mL of exosome-containing medium into the reservoir of a 15 mL 3KDa Amicon centrifugal filter.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,950 × g until 150 μL remains.
Repeat steps for remaining 15 mL supernatant.
Discard the flow through.
Transfer the concentrated medium from ‘Complete’ and ‘Starvation’ centrifugal filter reservoir to prelabeled microcentrifuge tubes.
Perform all centrifugation steps at 4°C.
Validate exosomes in the concentrated media by dynamic light scattering analysis using a Zetasizer Nano system.
Determine particle size by measuring Brownian motion of particles in the sample.
Turn on the Zetasizer Nano ZS 90 instrument and open the software.
Place around 100 μl of the sample in a quartz cuvette compatible with the instrument.
Place the cuvette in the instrument holder.
Start the particle size analysis option in the software.
Set up the required parameters such as refractive index and absorption for the material to be analyzed.
Disperse the solution in 1×PBS.
Set the refractive index to 1.338, as per the machine's preset option.
Input the number of measurements required (between 3–5).
Start the analysis on the software.
Wait for the temperature and other conditions to adjust automatically.
Obtain a graph between particle size (in nm) and intensity.
Identify the most abundant particles by their sharp and strong peak.
Expect peaks for exosomes to be in the range of 100–200 nm.
Rinse the cuvette with milliQ water after each measurement.
Repeat measurements for other samples as needed.
Copy the graph or raw values from the intensity option after completing a run.
Equilibrate two pre-labeled Izon qEV/35nm single-use columns with 150 μL 1× PBS (at a temperature of 18°C–25°C).
Load the concentrated ‘Complete’ and ‘Starvation’ medium onto the column.
Collect and discard the Buffer volume (1 mL).
Collect 100 μL fractions in pre-labeled microcentrifuge tubes (fractions 10-15).
Measure the absorbance of the collected fractions at 600 nm (for exosomes) and 280 nm (for proteins).
Incubate the columns at room temperature before starting the purification.
Estimate the protein amount in the whole cell lysates and purified exosomes using the Bradford assay.
Add 6× sample buffer after normalizing concentrations for all samples.
Heat samples at 85°C for 5 minutes to denature them.
Load equal amounts of protein per lane onto an SDS-PAGE gel.
Transfer proteins onto a 0.45 μm pore-sized PVDF membrane charged with methanol using the Tris Glycine transfer buffer in a wet transfer system at 4°C.
Block the membrane in a 5% skimmed milk solution prepared in 0.1% PBST at room temperature on a rocker for 1 hour.
Wash the membrane with 0.1% PBST three times, each for 5 minutes.
Dilute primary antibodies in 5% skimmed milk solution according to manufacturer’s instructions and add to the membrane.
Incubate the membrane with diluted primary antibodies at room temperature on a rocker for 2 hours.
Wash the membrane with 0.1% PBST three times, each for 5 minutes.
Perform blotting for proteins associated with exosomes like cysteine string protein (Csp) and Syntaxin 1A (Syx1A).
Dilute cysteine string protein (Csp) antibody at 1:1,000.
Dilute Syntaxin 1A (Syx1A) antibody at 1:500.
Gently rock the membrane incubated with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C.
Wash the membrane with 0.1% PBST 3–4 times for 5 minutes each to remove excess of the primary antibody.
Dilute HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies in 5% skimmed milk.
Add diluted secondary antibodies to the membrane and rock at room temperature for 1–2 hours to allow efficient binding.
Wash the membrane with 0.1% PBST 4–5 times for 5 minutes each.
Proceed to develop the blot on a ChemiDoc using an appropriate ECL detection system.
Load the fraction with the sharpest peak at 600 nm.
Load several fractions before and after the peak for analysis.
Load an equal amount of protein onto SDS-PAGE from cell lysates obtained under both complete medium and starvation conditions.
Ensure uniform transfection in both conditions.
Perform Western blot analysis on lysates, conditioned medium, and exosome fractions for the protein of interest.
Purify miRNAs loaded into exosomes.
Characterize purified miRNAs.
